Hi Alicia — thanks for the precise questions, happy to put concrete examples together. Short answers up front:

- Billing basis: aggregated input+output tokens (we report both separately in the invoice).
- Model deltas: we apply a model-class multiplier to the per-token base rate; embeddings can have a different multiplier than chat for premium models (we often price premium embeddings at a smaller uplift than premium chat due to compute profile).
- Commits: monthly smoothing within the 12-month commit. Overages billed at on-demand rates less the committed discount floor; we can define a true-up cadence (monthly or quarterly).

I’ve asked Marissa to draft a sample month and attach a starter term sheet / usage workbook. Marissa — can you include two scenarios (70/30 embed/chat and 90/10 embed/chat) and show the math for: base rate, premium multiplier, commit discount tiers (0-50M, 50-250M, 250M+), and overage handling? Also include how rounding is applied to token counts for billing.

Alicia — once Marissa and Rishi weigh in I’ll push the term sheet.

Jordan Blake

Hi all — attached is a starter term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and a simple workbook (cloudscale_usage_example.xlsx) that shows the two scenarios Jordan asked for. High level notes in the workbook and below.

Summary (sample month = 100,000,000 tokens):
- Measurement: we bill on aggregate tokens (input + output). Our instrumentation reports input/output so you can see composition. For the sample math we use raw token counts (no per-request rounding), but for billing we round each API call to the nearest 10 tokens to prevent microbilling noise.

- Base rates (on-demand): $0.000012 per token (chat baseline), $0.000007 per token (embeddings baseline) — these are illustrative and map to the term sheet.

- Premium multipliers (illustrative): premium chat = x2.0, premium embeddings = x1.4. We apply the multiplier per token category (chat tokens use chat multiplier, embed tokens use embed multiplier).

- Commit discount tiers (applied to the combined, post-multiplier token spend):
  * 0–50M tokens/month: 0% discount (on-demand)
  * 50–250M tokens/month: 15% discount on spend in this band
  * 250M+ tokens/month: 30% discount on spend above that threshold

- Overage policy: if you exceed the committed monthly band, overage is invoiced monthly at on-demand less a floor discount equal to your lowest committed tier (e.g., a customer with a 15% committed discount floor will have overages priced at on-demand - 15%). We also offer a quarterly true-up to reapply credits if annual consumption exceeds expectation.

Example (70/30 embed/chat, 100M tokens):
- Embeddings: 70M tokens x $0.000007 x 1.4 = $686.00
- Chat: 30M tokens x $0.000012 x 2.0 = $720.00
- Gross = $1,406.00 -> Apply band discounts per the tier math in the workbook -> Net invoice amount shown in sheet.

Notes / negotiation points you may want:
- We can tighten the premium multipliers for large commits (example: premium chat x2.0 -> x1.75 at 12-month $300K commit).
- We can price embeddings as a single blended SKU for simplified billing if that helps FP&A; that would slightly increase embedding unit price but simplify forecasting.
- Rounding policy above (nearest 10 tokens) reduces invoice noise on high QPS workloads.

Alicia — please confirm which scenario you want in an LOI and whether FP&A prefers per-SKU line items or a blended embed line. I can update the PDF into a DocuSign-ready term sheet once we land on those items.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Quick technical clarifications from infra/telemetry that should help finance reconcile numbers: 

- Token counting: we use the canonical tokenizer for each model family. Token counts reported in the console are exact; invoices apply the rounding policy Marissa noted (per request nearest 10 tokens). For batch embedding jobs our backend performs batching and deduplication at the prefix level — billing uses post-dedup token counts (so repeated identical inputs in the same batch are billed once).

- Embeddings compute profile: premium embedding models are GPU-bound for encoding, but per-request latency is often dominated by batch overhead. This is why premium embedding multiplier is lower (x1.4) compared to chat (x2.0) — the incremental cost is less dramatic.

- Storage & retention: embeddings vectors stored longer than 90 days incur a small monthly storage fee (we surfaced this in the term sheet). If CloudScale plans to store embeddings indefinitely we should surface that in the LOI.

If it helps I can produce a small sample API trace with token counts and the exact invoice line mapping.

-Rishi
